headline: Approved three FY '26 school budget transfers and a temporary surplus for part of 617 Lexington Street; tabled subcommittee meetings matter.
summary: Members approved three budget transfers requested by Mayor McCarthy, which leave a deficit of $864,596.08 in the FY '26 school budget. They also declared part of the second floor of 617 Lexington Street temporarily surplus for an outside group's after-hours use.
decisions: Approved the Consent Agenda, which included the prior minutes, retirements, resignations, and donations, with all in favor.
Approved moving the proposed March 2027 meetings to March 10, 2027 and March 24, 2027, with all in favor.
Approved the amended School Committee meeting calendar for 2027, with all in favor.
Tabled the School Committee subcommittee meetings matter to the next meeting, with all in favor.
Declared a portion of the second floor of 617 Lexington Street temporarily surplus for use by an outside organization, with all in favor.
Approved paying the bills on the warrant, with all in favor.
Approved the three FY '26 budget transfer requests made by Mayor McCarthy, with all in favor.
Approved removing the Waltham High School name from 617 Lexington Street, dedicating the building, and dedicating its west wing for Robert Eagle, with all in favor.

decision_evidence.quote: On motion of Ms. Wong-Bigelow, seconded by Mrs. AlJammal, to approve the Consent Agenda. All in favor.
On motion of Ms. DeJoannis, seconded by Mr. Tarallo, to move the proposed March meetings to March 10, 2027 and March 24, 2027. All in favor.
On motion by Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Ms. DeJoannis, to approve the amended School Committee Meeting Calendar for 2027. All in favor.
On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Ms. Wong-Bigelow, to table this matter to the next meeting. All in favor.

On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Mrs. AlJammal, to declare a portion of the second floor of the 617 Lexington Street building temporarily surplus for usage by an outside organization. All in favor.
On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Ms. Wong-Bigelow, to pay the bills on the warrant. All in favor.
On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Ms. Wong-Bigelow, to approve the three transfer requests made by Mayor McCarthy. All in favor.

On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Ms. DeJoannis, to remove the Waltham High School name from the front of the 617 Lexington Street building; to move forward with the dedication of the building, and to also dedicate the west wing of the building for Robert Eagle. All in favor.

 The monthly district enrollment report confirmed 5,45  2  students are currently enrolled 
 in Waltham Public Schools. 
 Ms. DeJoannis inquired about the projected increase of students next year at 
 Kennedy and how this will be addressed.  Dr. Mendonsa indicated administrators 
 have already begun to discuss how this increase will be handled and will continue to 
 work on this throughout the year. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Ms. Wong-Bigelow, seconded by  Mr. Tarallo, to hear from all 
 off-Committee members.  All in favor. 
 Kennedy Middle School administrators, Principal Kevin Gildea and Assistant 
 Principals Amy Woogmaster and Kate Sullivan, were present to share their school’s 
 improvement plan for the year.  Additionally, Mr. Kevin Tracey was introduced as the 
 school’s new interim principal. 
 Mr. Gildea explained how the School Improvement Plan was developed based on 
 data from last year.  While the school demonstrated an overall improvement in 
 iReady scores from the start of the year, literacy is the focus area for this year’s 
 improvement plan. 
 The Student Learning Goal for this year is “  All students  will increase their reading 
 skills by meeting their ‘typical growth goal’ as measured by iReady and students who 
 are 2 or more grade levels below grade level will meet their ‘stretch goal’ as 
 measured by iReady.”  The  Professional Practice Goal  is “  Teachers will expand their 
 instructional toolkit focusing on informational text to increase student literacy 
 performance” and the  School Culture Goal was identified  as “  We will improve the 
 school climate by establishing expectations to increase student Kindness, Motivation, 
 Success so that all students feel known, feel valued, and are empowered to 
 succeed.”  Information about the steps that will  be taken to achieve each goal along 
 with plans for progress monitoring were also provided. 
 The members asked some clarifying questions, provided feedback and wished Mr. 
 Gildea well in his upcoming retirement. 
 Mayor McCarthy asked Mr. Gildea if he believes the school would benefit from the 
 addition of another cluster and he confirmed it would, adding that either a new cluster 
 or the expansion of an already existing cluster would help. 
 McDevitt Middle School Principal Scott Lipman, accompanied by Assistant Principals 
 Jaime Wakefield and Tedd Markos, provided a summary of last year’s MCAS and 
 accountability improvement and noted the areas in which students are outperforming 
 state averages. 
 The middle school’s Student Learning Goal is “  Students  will demonstrate an 
 increased ability to independently comprehend rigorous texts across all grade levels 
 and content areas.”  The Professional Practice Goal was identified as “All teachers 
 and educators will consistently and intentionally implement accommodations and 
 scaffolds to support the needs of all students to ensure that students are 
 independently accessing tools which will enable them to comprehend grade level

 Ms. Wong-Bigelow, Ms. DeJoannis and Mayor McCarthy asked questions and

 Linda Flueckiger, Valor High School’s principal, shared the positive news about an 
 increase in the completion of modules by students last year.  She noted the 
 post-graduation shift between the Classes of 2025 and 2026.  Valor’s first year 
 graduates all intended to head into the workforce after graduation.  Last year, the 
 Class of 2026 planned to enter the workforce, enlist in the military, go to trade school, 
 or enroll in two or four year colleges. 
 Valor’s Growth and Support Plan listed its Student Learning Goal as “By the end of 
 the 2026-2027 school year, Valor High will improve student academic success and 
 engagement by strengthening attendance, academic accountability, classroom 
 academic supports, goal-setting, social-emotional learning, and school culture 
 through consistent advisory systems, instructional practices, and relationship-based 
 supports.” 
 The school’s Professional Practice Goal is “By the end of the 2026-2027 school year, 
 Valor High School will collaborate with WHS to share best practices that support 
 student engagement, attendance, academic success, and school connectedness, 
 while improving systems between Waltham High School and Valor High School to 
 ensure smooth referral, enrollment, and transition processes that also supports 
 student success.” 
 The Student Engagement / Family and Community Engagement Goal was identified 
 as “By the end of the 2026–2027 school year, Valor High will strengthen family and 
 community engagement by ensuring consistent communication, celebration, and 
 collaboration between the school and families, by expanding and strengthening 
 community partnerships, and formalizing structures for shared decision-making.” 
 The process for working toward each goal along with how progress will be monitored 
 was explained in detail by the principal. 
 Multiple questions were asked by the Committee relative to student attendance, 
 school flexibility, home visits, and family liaison support. 
 Nothing new was shared in this area. 
 Nothing new was shared at the meeting relative to this topic.

 Dr. Mendonsa reiterated that the new HVACR position at Waltham High remains 
 unfilled.  Students in Tech 2 are most impacted as they do not currently have a 
 teacher.  Additionally, freshmen CTE exploratory students have been informed that 
 HVACR will be removed from their exploratory rotation.  The superintendent shared 
 the current recommendation which includes keeping the position open so recruitment 
 efforts can continue, removing HVACR from this year’s exploratory program for either 
 first semester or the whole year if the position is not filled prior to the start of the 
 second semester, and eliminating HVACR from the lottery for Tech 1 placement if the 
 vacancy continues.  Looking ahead, if the position remains unfilled, the 
 recommendation is to offer HVACR Tech 1 every other year so enrolled students can 
 fill program requirements with the current staff. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mayor McCarthy, seconded by Ms.  DeJoannis, to hear from 
 Assistant Superintendent for Curriculum and Instruction Dr. Shannon Conley.  All in 
 favor. 
 All of the members asked questions and offered suggestions in an effort to determine 
 what options, if any, remain for filling the vacancy and how this might be impacted by 
 a different high school schedule next year.  The suggestions included: hire another 
 Ch. 74 teacher who could teach affiliated curriculum; explore online modules; contact 
 professional companies; explore double sessions; reach out to DESE for guidance, 
 and consider if a co-teaching model might work.  Dr. Conley confirmed the CTE PAC 
 has been informed and is attempting to assist.  She also discussed the other 
 suggestions and noted they will continue working toward a resolution. 
 The Waltham High School schedule committee will reconvene tomorrow to continue 
 its work. 
 Enrollment information as well as building capacity information for Kennedy and 
 McDevitt Middle Schools was provided to the Committee.  A request was made for a 
 more detailed visual to demonstrate specific class enrollment within the middle 
 schools. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Ms.  Wong-Bigelow, to table this 
 matter to the next meeting.  All in favor. 
 The School Committee reviewed a list of proposed meeting dates for 2027 and a 
 brief discussion followed. 
 VOTED:  On motion of  Ms. DeJoannis, seconded by Mr. Tarallo, to move the 
 proposed March meetings to March 10, 2027 and March 24, 2027.  All in favor.

 The Chair declared a recess at 9:37pm. 
 The School Committee reconvened at 9:41pm with all members, except Mrs. 
 Coleman, still present. 
 Mayor McCarthy read her letter which included a breakdown of surpluses and deficits 
 within the four school department accounts.  The mayor requested multiple funding 
 transfers: 
 ●  Funding transfer from the 5100 Account in the amount of $2,389,902.41 to be 
 applied to the deficits in the 5200 Account; 
 ●  Funding transfer from the 5400 Account in the amount of $17,125.05 to be 
 applied to the deficits in the 5200 Account, and 
 ●  Funding transfer from the 5500 Account in the amount of $10,996.38 to be 
 applied to the deficits in the 5200 Account. 
 After the transfers are completed, the overall deficit for the FY ‘26 School Department 
 Budget is $864,596.08.

 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Ms.  Wong-Bigelow, to approve the 
 three transfer requests made by Mayor McCarthy.  All in favor. 
 Mr. Zanghi asked how the deficit will be handled and the mayor advised 
 recommendations will be given and an outside auditors office will review. 
 Dr. Mendonsa received confirmation about how transfers can be made within school 
 department accounts.  Any transfers within the same account need to be approved 
 by the School Committee. 
 Mr. Tarallo thanked the City Council for approving the School Committee’s request to 
 rename the 617 Lexington Street building for former WPS Superintendent John 
 “Jack” Dadonna. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Ms.  DeJoannis, to remove the 
 Waltham High School name from the front of the 617 Lexington Street building; to 
 move forward with the dedication of the building, and to also dedicate the west wing 
 of the building for Robert Eagle.  All in favor. 
 Ms. DeJoannis inquired about reconvening the city-wide PTO meetings referenced at 
 the last School Committee meeting.  The Mayor confirmed she will handle facilitating 
 these and a short discussion about how they will be run, how matters can be 
 submitted for discussion and the School Committee’s involvement took place. 
 Ms. Wong-Bigelow asked when the survey about the district calendar for next year, 
 that was previously discussed last spring, will be circulated to the WPS community. 
 Ms. DeJoannis inquired about the next steps for obtaining student, staff and family 
 feedback since the district moved away from using Panorama surveys.  She asked 
 how the district plans to increase engagement. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. AlJammal, seconded by Ms. DeJoannis, to adjourn the 
 Regular Meeting at 10:03pm. All in favor.
